meta.title: "Add unsafe block" produces wrong syntax
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2025-08-25 and 2025-10-27; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2025-10-27. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1). These two builds cannot load a Cargo workspace with the local cargo 1.98 (--lockfile-path; attempt 1), so attempt 2 describes the crate with a rust-project.json (no cargo metadata call, no sysroot).
meta.notes: The missing_unsafe fix wraps only the call in 'unsafe { ... }'; when the call is the left operand of a binary or cast expression at the start of a statement, 'unsafe { f() } + 1' parses as a block statement followed by '+ 1'. The window is long because the repository has no weekly release tag between 2025-08-25 and 2025-10-27 (git tag --list).

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.source: comment by lnicola on 2025-10-04 (the valid-input example)

files.note: a rust-project.json describing the single library crate (root module src/lib.rs, edition 2021, no dependencies, no sysroot); it replaces the Cargo.toml of attempt 1 because these rust-analyzer builds cannot load a Cargo workspace with the local cargo 1.98 (they pass the unstable --lockfile-path, which cargo 1.98 rejects), and the case needs no std

repro.steps: Open src/lib.rs. The call f() of the unsafe fn in 'f() + 1' (line 5, character 4) is reported (missing unsafe, E0133). Apply its fix 'Add unsafe block' (requested for the range of the call). Reported: 'unsafe { f() } + 1', which does not parse as intended; expected '(unsafe { f() }) + 1' or equivalent. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have.

attempts.summary: Cargo project (Cargo.toml scaffold): invalid on both builds. Both 2025-08-25 and 2025-10-27 failed to load the workspace: 'Failed to read Cargo metadata with dependencies ... cargo metadata exited with an error: unexpected argument --lockfile-path' (they pass --lockfile-path with -Zunstable-options when the toolchain is new enough, and the local cargo 1.98 no longer has that flag), so no diagnostics were computed ('no diagnostic matching {code: E0133}; have []').

First run of attempt 2 (rust-project.json), voided: both builds loaded and indexed the crate, but published no diagnostics for src/lib.rs at all (no publishDiagnostics message in the session logs), so the edit spec, which selected the fix through the published E0133 diagnostic, requested no code action ('no diagnostic matching {code: E0133}; have []'). The rerun selects the fix by its range (the call f() in 'f() + 1'); rust-analyzer computes the fixes of a range on request, independent of published diagnostics. Same project, same probe.
attempts.verdict: void (no published diagnostics to select the fix)
